newsitem.title: INDONESIA: S.E. Asia takes first step towards cocoa contract.
newsitem.headline: S.E. Asia takes first step towards cocoa contract.

text.p: Southeast Asian cocoa producers, meeting here at a two-day conference, agreed on Tuesday on the need to set up a regional trading contract to reduce dependence on foreign pacts.

"All of us agreed it is a good thing," Mohamed Musa Jamil of the Malaysian Cocoa Board told Reuters after the end of the first day of discussions, adding that the contract was earmarked for implementation by the turn of the century.
Conference delegates, however, said much work was needed before the contract, covering the seven members of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), could be formed.
"We want to make an inventory of the very important factors for this contract," conference chairman Suharyo Husen of Indonesia's Agriculture Ministry told Reuters.
"The contract will be in the interest of all ASEAN members. We want to increase our trade...with common regulations and control (over) quality and to improve our competitiveness."
As a first step, Jamil said host Indonesia had been put in charge of setting up a regional team to study the formation of an arbitration body to support the ASEAN cocoa contract.
"Each member country will be represented in the team which will begin work immediately," he said adding that the contract was earmarked for implementation by the year 2000.
"The team will formulate details of the contract such as what needs to be done and so on. In the end, it has to come up with a contract that everybody can use," he said.
Another Indonesian delegate said the meeting agreed on the need for a common contract but added that ASEAN members must decide what shape it takes.
"We will need to work out the shape of the common contract," he said.
Government and private sector representatives from Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Malaysia -- which together with Brunei and Vietnam comprise ASEAN -- attended the meeting.
The move to set up the common contract is being spearheaded by Malaysia in a bid to bridge the quality gap among Southeast Asian cocoa producers and narrow existing price disparities.
Indonesia and Malaysia are the region's top two producers.
Siswoputranto, executive director of the Indonesian Cocoa Association, said Indonesia had to be cautious.

"There has been a political decision by ASEAN on the contract, and we need to fulfil it but we need to be cautious. The ASEAN contract should be an alternative to contracts in London and New York," he told reporters.
He said a common regional contract would allow independent Southeast Asian countries to avoid dependence on foreign pacts.
"When we are doing business with Vietnam, for instance, why should we be using London contracts," he said. "It is the same with other intra-ASEAN business (in cocoa)."
Delegates said an ASEAN contract would offer other advantages such as providing dispute-solving mechanisms within the region.
"The problem now is whether the contract we want to set up will gain the confidence of the international cocoa community," Siswoputranto said. "That's the key."
